items.headline: Silicon Valley Power software contract up to $3.79M listed
items.summary: The November 10 City Council agenda listed an action to delegate authority to the City Manager to sign an agreement with cQuant.io, Inc. for generation resource modeling software for Silicon Valley Power. Maximum compensation would be $3,791,855 over a ten-year term.

items.headline: 251-unit Eden Housing project at 10333 N. Wolfe Road on Planning Commission agenda
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 10 agenda listed Architectural and Site Approval and Tree Removal Permits for a 251-unit residential development by Eden Housing, with site and trail improvements. The plan calls for removing and replacing 117 protected trees.

items.headline: 363 apartments proposed to replace offices on Stevens Creek Boulevard
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 10 agenda listed The Hanover Company's request for a 363-unit apartment development at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, replacing existing office buildings. The site covers Sites 5 and 6 of the city's Housing Element priority housing sites, and the project relies on SB 330 and state density bonus law. The agenda also listed a parcel map and a tree removal permit.

items.headline: Primrose preschool for up to 192 kids proposed on Homestead Road
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a Special Development Permit to demolish a vacant commercial building at 855 E. Homestead Road and build a 2-story, 16,000-square-foot childcare and preschool for up to 192 children. The 1.11-acre project, with CASCO of Primrose Schools as applicant, includes a new eight-foot masonry wall along the western and part of the southern property lines.

items.headline: Sunnyvale parking rules for housing up for rewrite citywide
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a recommendation to the City Council on an ordinance to repeal and replace Chapter 19.46 (Parking) of the zoning code, revising residential off-street parking requirements. It would also amend the Downtown, Lawrence Station, and El Camino Real specific plan chapters, the definitions chapter, and the Dual Urban Opportunity Housing chapter.

items.headline: Historic Commission agenda: 1,200 sq ft backyard unit at 1391 Washington Street
items.summary: The November 5 Historical and Landmarks Commission agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street, a Historic Resource Inventory property. The request (PLN26-00020) is a Significant Property Alteration / Architectural Review and was listed as categorically exempt from environmental review.

items.headline: Historic commission to pick member for preservation ordinance consultant panel
items.summary: The November 5 Historical and Landmarks Commission agenda included selecting one commissioner to serve on the review board choosing a consultant for the city's Historic Preservation Ordinance Update. The ordinance update could change how Santa Clara protects its historic properties.

items.headline: Tech Park project's traffic and redwood removal drew concerns from council and neighbors
items.summary: Staff said the project adds a net 1,368 daily trips, and required mitigation is limited to a new mid-block crosswalk and crossing upgrades on Campbell Technology Park. Left-turn queuing at Curtner/White Oaks/Camden is already over capacity, and the city has no objective standard to require fixes. Paseo de Palomas residents asked to keep the redwoods along the shared fence line, and council members questioned why they must all be removed. Developers agreed to record easements for a possible future Highway 17 pedestrian/bike bridge, but no feasibility study is funded yet.
